objectives: Recognise the silent t pattern in taught words.
Hear listen, castle, and whistle without an extra /t/ sound.
Distinguish the spoken word from its conventional spelling.
Keep t in the written word.
concepts: In the taught words listen, castle, and whistle, t is silent.
The spelling retains t even though it is not pronounced.
The surrounding sounds and word meaning identify the word.
Silent-letter patterns are learned from examples.

definitions.definition: A written letter that is not pronounced.
A letter or group of letters representing a sound.
A speech sound that can distinguish one word from another.

workedExamples.solution: Do not insert a /t/ sound between s and e.
Castle has a silent t; cattle pronounces t.
Keep t in spelling, but do not pronounce it.

commonMistakes: Deleting t from spelling because it is silent.
Guessing without listening to the word.
keyTakeaways: t is silent in the taught words.
